4. **Category:** edge-case / **Severity:** medium — AC-4 names a completed `code` row, but the existing evidence floor accepts either `code` or `external_code`. Define the cascade's Stage-2 set centrally and state whether `external_code` is intentionally outside the cascade.

Have the shared reader return a typed result distinguishing `current`, `foreign`, `unattributed`, and `invalid/missing`.

6. **Category:** approach / **Severity:** medium — AC-2 calls the required values evidence, but the proposed predicate permits trivially fabricated metadata such as `provider: ""`, whitespace-only excerpts, or arbitrary `recorded_by`.

findings.finding: The Stage-1 remediation advertised a command with no --run-id, which _parse_args marks required — argparse exits 2 on usage. The identical defect external round 3.2 caught (--from spec-reviewer); only the adapter half was fixed. The pinning test regexed --from only, so it green-lit a command that does not run.
findings.suggestion: Give stage_one_precedes_stage_two the run_id parameter and emit it; strengthen the test to shlex the command out of the message and feed it to the real _parse_args.

findings.finding: stage_one_precedes_stage_two was satisfied by gates.spec.status == completed alone, no evidence required — so the HARD-GATE this run exists to make provable was the one row that could still be asserted rather than evidenced, with carries_evidence sitting 40 lines above it.
findings.suggestion: Treat completed as satisfying only when carries_evidence(spec_entry), with its own message so the repair stays distinct from the not-completed case.

findings.finding: F11.md — the runtime prompt loaded AT the failing step — still enumerated five review types, so an agent reading it while the gate reports '1 review type(s) still unanswered: spec' is reading an enumeration that denies the row exists. SKILL.md, iteration-reviews.md, F5c.md and hooks-and-pipeline.md were updated; this one was not. Neither new failure mode was mentioned either.
findings.suggestion: Update to the six-row vocabulary and add the evidence-floor and Stage-1-ordering failure modes with their repairs.

findings.finding: The no-record branch passed REVIEW_TYPES to _remediation, which renders 'close all {n} at once' — telling the operator 5 for a close-missing that will close 6. A site the P4 inventory missed.

_repair_or_reject and review_record_ops.repair_companion both read record['reviews'] directly, bypassing _section — whose docstring says routing in ONE place is what keeps the split from leaking. Not live today (both require --marker-status, restricted to MARKER_TYPES) but a gate type carrying a marker would read {} and produce a nonsense message.
findings.suggestion: Export a section-aware accessor from review_record_core and use it at both call sites.

findings.finding: Three re-exports (_CODE_REVIEW_TYPES, FLOORED_COMPLEXITIES, carries_evidence) with noqa markers and a comment asserting 'existing importers and tests resolve them at this module'. Measured repo-wide: zero references outside review_record_floor.py. The measurement that legitimately retired declared_removals was not run here.
findings.suggestion: Drop the three re-exports and the justifying comment.

findings.finding: Dead sys.path bootstrap in review_record_floor.py (new file) and silent_revert.py — neither imports lib.* any more (silent_revert's only lib import moved to silent_revert_detect.py in this diff), and .common performs the identical bootstrap. The sibling extraction silent_revert_filters.py correctly carries none.
findings.suggestion: Delete the bootstrap, the unused import sys, and the accompanying noqa: E402 markers.

findings.finding: attributed_declared_removals accepted the per-run block only when isinstance(list); any other present-but-wrong shape fell through to the shared file and could return silence — the same 'cannot tell none from unreadable' condition the malformed branch was just changed to report. The F5c entry is the home operators hand-write, so it is the likelier place to get the shape wrong.
findings.suggestion: Report when per_run is present but not a list, symmetric with the malformed rule.

findings.finding: Two new tests git init a repo with NO commits, so check_no_silent_revert returns at its pre-flight ('main does not resolve') and the clean-run path the tests name is never reached. The assertions hold on the skip result. Same shape as the AC-7 test the run itself found non-discriminating.
findings.suggestion: Commit a file so the comparison actually runs, and assert the result is not a skip.

findings.finding: Residual of accepted AC-1b: the durable home now carries the gates' only surviving evidence on a behind branch, but nothing on the producing side checks it was filled in. An agent following F5b/F5c without reading the new prose learns about it as a post-commit F11 red after ensure_current has already rewound the shared file — at the last step of the run.
findings.suggestion: Emit a non-fatal warning when a medium/large entry carries neither block, moving discovery back to F5c where the data is still in hand.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The spec row can be recorded by following the documented command. — DISPROVED. The one documented way to record the new spec row could not consume the spec-reviewer's actual output: --from code-reviewer routes to from_code_reviewer, which requires a top-level 'review' array, while spec-reviewer.md pins the Stage-1 contract as {stage, verdict, spec_citations, summary} on PASS and REJECT alike. Handing the reply over verbatim exits 1 payload_unreadable. Every test substituted a code-reviewer payload, hiding it. The gate that exists to make Stage 1 provable made FABRICATING its evidence easier than recording it — confirmed by this very run, which hit the error and hand-transformed its payload.

Claim under doubt: -w to -b diverges only on de-indent, harmlessly. — DISPROVED. It is a HUNK-BOUNDARY effect, not a line-equality one. -b marks a strict superset as changed, and under -U0 a changed line JOINS two hunks an unchanged line separates. A de-indent to column 0 between two regions merges them, so unexplained_by_edit lets an added line from region B vouch for a deleted line in region A — the unbounded matching replacement_hunks' own docstring rejects, re-entered through the back door. Monotone: -b hunks are never narrower, and wider hunks can only suppress more.

Claim under doubt: The gates design breaks no reader. — DISPROVED for tomorrow's writer. _validate_gates rejected unknown gate keys exactly as the webui rejects unknown reviews keys — but schema_version is frozen at 1 by design and GATE_TYPES is documented as where future stages go. The day it gains a second member, new-writer records read as schema-INVALID to every reader on the old constant, and the gate tells the operator to 'repair or delete' a healthy, immutable, git-tracked, never-evicted history. That is section 1.3's failure mode reproduced inside the monorepo, and the plugin cache makes old-and-new readers routine.

Claim under doubt: An absent gates section is answerable by close-missing. — DISPROVED in composition. stage_one_precedes_stage_two is not complexity-gated, so any run that recorded code=completed BEFORE this lands — every in-flight worktree, whose code row is already terminal and immutable — reaches F11 with gates absent and is hard-failed. All three exits are bad: invent evidence for spec, --force-rewrite a real code row to not_run and destroy its findings, or delete the record. No migration path for 'Stage 1 ran, before there was a row for it'.

Claim under doubt: The evidence floor cannot be cleared without evidence. — DISPROVED. carries_evidence was defeated by --recorded-by <anything>: the flag has no choices, and the predicate checked non-blank-and-not-'none' while its own message calls the trace 'a recorded_by naming an ADAPTER'. Combined with the high finding this stops being theoretical — the honest route for spec was broken, and this flag is the first thing an agent finds when --from exits 1.

Claim under doubt: The F5c warning moves discovery earlier. — PARTLY DISPROVED. It used `any`, so carrying EITHER block silenced the warning about the OTHER — and F11 then hard-failed on the absent one after ensure_current had already rewound the shared file: the exact discovery-too-late sequence the warning exists to move.

Claim under doubt: The present-but-wrong-shape gap was fixed. — DISPROVED for the siblings. It was fixed only in attributed_declared_removals. validate_iterate_entry does no shape check on the extra keys, so a string test_completeness is accepted at F5c, silently ignored at F11, and produces 'the F5c entry carries no test_completeness either' — false, and pointing at a repair already performed.

Claim under doubt: The F5c entry is a durable home. — PARTLY DISPROVED. AC-1b relocated the load-bearing evidence to the ONE artifact with a hard TTL: iterates/ is a 50-entry recency cache (already AT the cap), while reviews.json and the event log are never evicted. It does not bite the run's own F11 — the entry is the newest — but after eviction AC-3's message 'F5c did not run' is a false statement for an aged-out run.

attributed_declared_removals()` treats every non-current `iterate_latest` state as harmless when the foreign/malformed/missing snapshot contains no declarations: it returns `([], None)`. Consequently, `check_silent_revert_for_run()` can pass or skip on a clean tree without reporting that the declarations source was missing, malformed, unattributed, or belonged to another run. AC-1 explicitly requires every caller, including `declared_removals`, to fail closed on every non-`current` state and provide repair guidance. The current behavior only reports a foreign source if there happened to be declarations to disregard.
findings.suggestion: Return a non-current-state problem unconditionally whenever no valid per-run F5c `declared_removals` list is available, including an explicitly empty list as the durable “no declarations” evidence. Make `check_silent_revert_for_run()` turn that problem into a blocking F11 failure rather than a conditional warning.

findings.finding: test_no_declarations_anywhere_stays_silent` codifies the fail-open behavior above by asserting that a foreign `iterate_latest` with no declarations must not fail or disclose anything. This is contrary to AC-1’s requirement that all three readers fail closed for all non-`current` attribution states, so the test suite would reject a compliant implementation that fixes the production defect.
findings.suggestion: Replace this test with cases asserting a blocking result for missing, malformed, unattributed, and foreign shared snapshots when the F5c entry lacks `declared_removals`; retain a passing case only when the per-run F5c entry explicitly carries `declared_removals: []`.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The attribution reader and the other AC implementations are broadly aligned with the specification, but the silent-revert declaration path still intentionally bypasses the required fail-closed contract in a concrete non-current-state case.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
